newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 30.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 30.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$19.15 (+0.09)

BHP has assured investors it will achieve a much higher level of performance by year 2000, but it has again downplayed hopes of an immediate improvement. BHP managing director John Prescott said in a television interview broadcast on Sunday that he took considerable blame for the steel, mining and petroleum group's recent woes. BHP is also due to hold its annual results briefing for analysts in Melbourne on Monday.

Wesfarmers Ltd has revealed it held unsuccessful discussions with Imperial Chemical Industries Plc (ICI) this week to make a takeover bid for ICI Australia Ltd. Wesfarmers said in statement released to the Australian Stock Exchange late on Friday it had discussed with ICI Plc the possible purchase of a 19.9 percent stake in ICI Australia followed by a takeover offer. But ICI rejected the overture to a bid Wesfarmers described as superior to ICI's global offer proceeds.

Carpenter Pacific Resources NL said on Thursday that it had agreed to give landowners a 10 percent free carried stake in the exploration licence at the Mt Kare gold prospect in the highlands of Papua New Guinea.

Simeon Wines Ltd said late on Friday it would provide an alternative takeover offer for Australian Vintage Ltd, which would give AustVin shareholders a higher cash component for their shares. AustVin directors had said they would unanimously recommend that shareholders accept the revised offer.

Woodside Petroleum Ltd, operator of the North West Shelf oil and gas project offshore Western Australia, said late on Friday it had received a joint development proposal from the operator of the neighbouring Gorgon gas prospect.
Coal & Allied Industries Ltd said on Friday it was disappointed employees at its Hunter Valley Number One mine had voted to continue a two-week old strike.

Green's Foods Ltd said late on Friday that earnings for the second half of the 1996/97 year ending June 30 would be below expectations, but that the result for the year would be higher than the previous year.
